title: Shilpa Shirodkar Returns to Bollywood After 26 Years With Malamaal Weekly 2
excerpt: The 90s star and Mahesh Babu's sister-in-law signs on for the comedy sequel alongside Raveena Tandon, Parineeti Chopra and Paresh Rawal.
body:
• Shilpa Shirodkar has signed Malamaal Weekly 2, marking her first Hindi film since Gaja Gamini in 2000
  • The sequel also stars Raveena Tandon, Parineeti Chopra and Paresh Rawal, directed by Amit Joshi
  • The film is not a direct sequel — it features new characters and settings but retains the original's comedic premise

Shilpa Shirodkar, one of the defining screen presences of 1990s Bollywood, is making her return to Hindi cinema after a 26-year absence. The actor has signed on for Malamaal Weekly 2, the sequel to the 2006 Priyadarshan-directed comedy, according to an exclusive report by Bollywood Hungama.

Shirodkar's last Hindi film was the late M.F. Husain's Gaja Gamini (2000), making this one of the longest comeback gaps in recent Bollywood history.

An Ensemble Cast Takes Shape

Malamaal Weekly 2 is assembling an impressive cast. Raveena Tandon and Parineeti Chopra were confirmed last week, while Paresh Rawal — who appeared in the original — has also given his nod. The film will be directed by Amit Joshi, known for Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya (2024).

"Shilpa loved her part and the overall script. The makers were keen to have her on board; however, she has not signed films in a long time, though she keeps getting offers at regular intervals. Hence, the makers of Malamaal Weekly 2 were on cloud nine when Shilpa Shirodkar showed interest."

— Source close to the production, via Bollywood Hungama

The makers are reportedly still looking to cast additional prominent actors in key roles, suggesting the ensemble will grow further before production begins.

Not a Direct Sequel

According to production sources, Malamaal Weekly 2 is not a direct sequel to the original. The characters and setting will be entirely different, but the film retains the comedic DNA of its predecessor — a group of greedy villagers who go to outlandish lengths to get their hands on a large sum of money.

The original Malamaal Weekly, released in March 2006, was directed by Priyadarshan and starred Ritesh Deshmukh, Paresh Rawal and Rajpal Yadav in a story about a village where a lottery winner dies, leading to elaborate schemes to hide the death from authorities.

Shirodkar's Journey Back to Films

Shirodkar built a prominent career in the 1990s, working with legends including Dev Anand in Return of Jewel Thief and Dilip Kumar in the unreleased Kalinga. She comes from a family of performers — her mother Gangu Bai and grandmother Meenakshi Shirodkar were both actors, and her older sister Namrata Shirodkar had her own film career before marrying Telugu superstar Mahesh Babu.

In recent years, Shirodkar has appeared on television, including a stint on Bigg Boss 18 in late 2025, and had a supporting role in the pan-India supernatural thriller Jatadhara (2025). She has been candid about her desire to work, telling interviewers: "Main sabko bolti hoon ki bhai mujhe kaam chahiye."

She has spoken positively about the evolution of the industry, noting: "Today cinema has changed, writing has changed, there is work for everyone across borders, across age groups, across genders. For me, I feel I'm in the best time of making movies."

Comic Capers Making a Comeback

Malamaal Weekly 2 joins a wave of comedy sequels in development, including Dhamaal 4, Bhagam Bhag 2, Hera Pheri 3 and Golmaal 5. The trend reflects a renewed appetite for ensemble comedies in Bollywood, following the success of the romantic genre's revival in 2025.
